OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan (kt CPO)
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is flat on the last actual; from FY2027E we roll in part of the immature pipeline. FY2025 CPO sales were 105.858 kt [F1] on production of 104.871 kt [F5]. The nucleus is 16,139 ha, of which 4,342 ha (27%) is immature and 11,797 ha mature [S2 p.88]; own FFB was 161.436 kt on the mature area, a normal 13.7 t/ha, so the immature block is a genuine volume pipeline rather than a maturity ceiling. At 13.7 t/ha the 4,342 ha would add about 59.5 kt of FFB at full maturity, or about 13.5 kt of CPO at the 22.7% oil extraction rate the mill shows (104.871 kt CPO on 461.117 kt FFB [F5, F7]) - roughly 13% of current sales. Two offsets cap the net path: 3,957 ha of the mature area is older than fourteen years and due for replanting [S2 p.88], which removes mature area as the young palms come in, and the 65% bought-fruit share (461.117 kt processed against 161.436 kt own [F7, F8]) depends on catchment supply that no filing guides. We therefore take about half the gross maturation over five years, +1.4% a year to FY2030E, and hold it flat thereafter. The mill is not near a throughput cap: S6 gives it 120 t/h, or roughly 600-790 kt/yr of FFB against 461 kt processed, 58-77% utilisation [S6]. The 11-Nov-2026 GAPKI warning that El Nino could take up to 3m tonnes off Indonesian output in 2027 is an industry aggregate, not company guidance, and is carried in the bear (volume x0.95), not in the base [S5].

assumptions.label: Realised CPO price / World Bank benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual and the last twelve months, held flat. FY2025 is audited and unambiguous: Rp14.115m per tonne [F3] at the FY2025 average rate of Rp16,448 per dollar is USD 858.2/t against the deck FY2025 benchmark of USD 1,007/t, a ratio of 0.852 [fund record]. That 0.852 is measured against the pre-2026 World Bank Pink Sheet series, which the deck itself flags as re-based from January 2026 (fund record basis: the annual averages and the 2026 monthly tape are not perfectly homogeneous), so it is not the like-for-like multiplier for a FY2026+ forecast. The like-for-like test is the twelve months to September 2026: LTM revenue is Rp2,480.5bn [S0] and CPO carried 64.9% of FY2025 revenue (Rp1,494.2bn of Rp2,303.9bn at the F3/F1 price and volume) [S3 p.91, F17, F18], so CPO revenue of roughly Rp1,610bn on about 106 kt is Rp15.2m per tonne, against the deck 9M-2026 average of USD 1,131/t at the 2026 rate of Rp17,570 - Rp19.9m per tonne - i.e. 0.76. That is the same wedge the desk already carries on LSIP (0.758) and it is structural, not cautious: these are domestic sales at the administratively set Harga Referensi/KPB, which lags the export print, while the levy and duty (USD 246.36/t for November 2026) sit on the exported benchmark and on no domestic tonne. Sanity check on total revenue: 0.76 x 1,135 x 17.57 = Rp15.15m per tonne, +7.4% on FY2025, which with flat tonnes reproduces the 9M-2026 revenue growth of 10.9% [S0]; at the old-series 0.852 the model would print about 20% revenue growth, which the filings contradict. Held flat rather than faded: holding is the last-actual rule.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic market obligation or price cap applies to palm oil; the DMO regimes on coal and cooking oil (minyakita) price caps apply to packers of branded cooking oil, not to a CPO mill selling to refiners. Set to zero.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (1.0 - no overburden analogue)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost is expressed per tonne of CPO, so the intensity factor is 1.0 and the whole cash cost sits in cost_per_bcm. A plantation has no strip-ratio equivalent; the FFB-to-CPO ratio is in the cost, not in a volume multiplier.

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR, ex-royalty and ex-D&A)
assumptions.basis: Built from the FY2025 cost-of-sales note, not from a ratio of revenue: FFB purchases Rp963.561bn [F15] plus the palm share of the shared estate cost, bearing in mind note 36. The shared estate lines are harvest and transport Rp108.202bn, processing Rp68.216bn, fertiliser Rp43.128bn and mature-plantation maintenance Rp26.032bn, Rp245.378bn in total. Note 36 shows the rubber segment alone carried COGS of Rp479.434bn on revenue of Rp541.508bn [S3 p.102]; against its own lump purchases of Rp329.719bn [F16] that leaves Rp149.715bn of processing and estate cost on rubber, so Rp65.758bn of the shared pool belongs to rubber and had been sitting in the CPO cost. We move it out on the segment COGS evidence: palm shared cost becomes Rp179.833bn and the FY2025 CPO cash cost Rp1,143.394bn on 105.858 kt [F1], or Rp10.801m per tonne (previously Rp11.422m). The residual splits by behaviour, because the company buys 65% of the FFB it mills at a formula price: the FFB line is Rp9.103m per tonne of CPO and moves with the CPO price (64.5% pass-through), while the Rp1.699m of estate cost moves with Indonesian inflation only. So unit cost = 1.699 x 1.025^(t-2025) + 9.103 x (ASP_t / 14.115), priced off the deck CPO series and the deck rupiah path - the FY2027E step is the deck El Nino spike (USD 1,240/t) lifting the FFB purchase price, and the FY2028E retreat is the price falling back. Beyond FY2030E the cost escalates at 2.5% IDR inflation, the same rate as the deck long run, so the real spread is flat.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cash cost
assumptions.basis: Not used: no fuel driver is linked for palm oil. Set to zero so the input cannot leak a coal-shaped adjustment into the cost base.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit
assumptions.basis: Zero: every cash-cost component of note 29 is already inside cost_per_bcm, so a second per-tonne bucket would double count.

assumptions.label: Royalty / export levy rate
assumptions.basis: Zero for this name: all sales are domestic (two Indonesian refinery customers take 62.35% of revenue [F19, S3 p.91]) and the CPO export levy is levied on the exporter at shipment, so it never reaches this P&L. No royalty or levy line exists in note 29 [S3 p.91].

assumptions.label: Non-CPO revenue (crumb rubber, palm kernel, FFB trading, compost)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 non-CPO revenue is Rp809.7bn: total revenue Rp2,303.919bn [F18] less CPO revenue of Rp1,494.2bn (105.858 kt at Rp14.115m [F1, F3]). Within it crumb rubber is Rp541.508bn [F17] and the balance is palm kernel, traded FFB and compost. The block is held flat in FY2026E and grown at 2.5% IDR inflation thereafter, because its largest line is shrinking: crumb rubber production fell from 31,841 t in 2023 to 23,733 t in 2024 and 14,779 t in 2025, -54% in two years [S2 p.90], and the 816 ha of immature rubber is not enough to reverse that. Kernel volumes can grow with the CPO volume path, but we do not have a kernel price series and will not assume a rubber recovery that the annual report contradicts. A flat real block is the honest base; the growth case is in the bull, not here.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on non-CPO revenue
assumptions.basis: Solved from the note and reconciled to note 36, not assumed: FY2025 COGS of Rp1,675.864bn [S0] less depreciation in COGS of Rp38.821bn and bearer-plant amortisation of Rp14.228bn [F12, F14] gives Rp1,622.815bn of cash COGS. Of that, Rp1,143.394bn is the CPO cash cost after moving the rubber share of the shared estate pool (see cost_per_bcm), leaving Rp479.421bn against Rp809.700bn of non-CPO revenue, a 40.8% gross margin. That now brackets the filing: note 36 shows the rubber segment at COGS of Rp479.434bn on Rp541.508bn of revenue, an 11.5% margin on the segment as presented, while the non-CPO block here also carries palm kernel, which the note books inside the palm segment. The previous 48.9% margin was too high because Rp65.758bn of rubber processing and estate cost sat in the CPO pool; the block margin is now a blend of a thin rubber line and a kernel line, not a margin above the segment that dominates it.

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: Full-charge D&A of Rp66.933bn: fixed-asset depreciation of Rp52.705bn [F12] plus bearer-plant amortisation of Rp14.228bn charged to cost of sales [F14], on 105.858 kt [F1] = Rp632,290 per tonne. The pack carries only Rp13.883bn of D&A (the G&A allocation) [S0], a fifth of the real charge, because the IDX filing reports the direct cash-flow method; the fact above restates the history line to the note. Escalated at 2.5% IDR inflation as capex is refreshed. The first forecast period is FY2026E and this value already carries one year of escalation (Rp632,290 x 1.025 = Rp648,097); the engine reads the input as given across FY2026E-FY2030E and applies its own escalation only beyond the last explicit year, so no second 2.5% lands inside FY2026E - the FY2026E D&A line of Rp69.3bn is Rp648,097 x 107.0kt.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex of Rp119.575bn [S0, cash-flow statement] on 105.858 kt [F1] = Rp1,129,585 per tonne: replanting of immature palms, nursery and mill/vehicle replacement. Held at the last actual in real terms and escalated at 2.5% IDR inflation; no expansion capex is assumed because the new controlling shareholder has published no investment plan for this asset, and inventing one would be unsourced drift in either direction. The first forecast period is FY2026E and this value already includes one year of escalation (Rp1,129,585 x 1.025 = Rp1,157,825); the engine applies the input as given across the explicit forecast and escalates only beyond the last explicit year, so the FY2026E capex line of Rp123.9bn is Rp1,157,825 x 107.0kt with no second 2.5%.

assumptions.label: Expansion capex
assumptions.basis: Zero: no announced expansion beyond the immature planting already inside sustaining capex.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Last actual, not the three-year average the engine seeds: FY2025 operating working capital of Rp237.595bn [S0] on revenue of Rp2,303.919bn is 10.31%; the FY2022-FY2024 average is distorted by the Rp335bn of inventory held in 2022 when CPO prices spiked. Held at 10.31%.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective rate of 22.68% (tax Rp94.618bn on pre-tax Rp417.183bn [S0]), in line with the 22% statutory rate in Law 7/2021 and the temporary differences in the LK tax reconciliation. Held at the last actual.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt
assumptions.basis: Two different rates, stated once so they are not confused. This input prices interest on the opening debt in the P&L (interest expense = debt[-1] x a.cost_of_debt): FY2025 interest expense of Rp29.821bn on opening debt of Rp594.824bn is 5.01% and the three-year average is 6.11% [S0], so 6.11% is what the interest line carries and no new debt is assumed. The WACC does not read this input: the engine prices debt there at the macro deck risk-free rate of 7.45% plus the corporate debt spread of 2.00%, i.e. 9.45% pre-tax [fund record rf_idr and debt_spread_corp]. That is an rf-plus-spread default for an Indonesian borrower, not this company's realised rate, and at a debt weight of 6.3% the two rates differ by about a tenth of a percentage point on the WACC.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default from the pack, 0.57% [S0]; immaterial at the cash balances this company runs (Rp97bn at 30-Sep-2026 [S0]).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from Rp594.8bn to Rp339.8bn in FY2025 and to Rp171.1bn by 30-Sep-2026 [S0], so the company is amortising, not borrowing. No refinancing need is visible.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero for the recurring block. The half year to June 2026 carried a Rp26.4bn gain on the change in fair value of biological assets [S4 p.7: "Perubahan nilai wajar atas aset biologis 26.396.456.000"], against a Rp1.1bn loss in H1-2025, and it is the largest single non-operating item in the half. It is excluded on two grounds: it is non-recurring (a mark on the standing crop at the reporting date, which the 2025 accounts show at a similar order of magnitude but with no guidance for the future) and it is non-operating (it is recognised in other income and expense, not in the mill trading result). The recurring non-operating piece is interest, which is modelled explicitly on the debt line.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Engine default from the pack, 0.25% [S0]; minority interests are Rp3.9bn of a Rp1,267bn equity base at 30-Jun-2026 [S4].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 40%, the three-year average of declared DPS over EPS (FY2023 92/245 = 37.5%, FY2024 170/282 = 60.3%, FY2025 90/412 = 21.8%; DPS from the pack [S0], EPS from the audited accounts [S2]). The LK states no fixed payout ratio - dividends are whatever the RUPS decides [S2 p.100] - so the average of what has actually been declared is the honest base. The new controlling shareholder has owned the asset only since May 2026, so its capital-allocation preference is unproven and is flagged in section 6 rather than modelled.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 781.25m shares, unchanged since the 2019 IPO; the company has never done a rights issue or a split [S0, S2].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%, the macro deck long-run Indonesian inflation scalar [fund record inflation_idr_lt]: the CPO deck long run and the IDR cost base both escalate at 2.5%, so real free cash flow is flat and 2.5% is the nominal growth the terminal value carries. Using the 4% house default would assume a real 1.5% perpetuity on a crop whose yield is flat and whose land bank is fixed at 19,952 ha [F9].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 12.3% of revenue, the H1-2026 run rate, carried because no filing sources the step-up as one-off. H1-2026 G&A was Rp131.116bn and selling Rp10.841bn on revenue of Rp1,116.558bn [S4 p.7]; depreciation inside G&A was Rp4.601bn [S4 p.58], so ex-D&A opex is Rp137.356bn, 12.3% of H1 revenue, or Rp274.7bn annualised. The increase is in salaries and allowances, Rp84.031bn against Rp44.863bn in H1-2025, a recurring cash line [S4 p.85]; security, insurance and utilities rose with it. There is no transaction or integration cost line in note 30 and no page of S4 discloses one, so the previous 7.70% (which was the FY2025 audited ex-D&A ratio) cannot stand as the forecast: it assumed the H1 jump halves without a source. H1-2025 was 52.6% of FY2025 revenue, so the half-year is a fair annual run rate and the ratio is held flat across the forecast. The alternative - a fade back to 7.7% - is unsourced and would be the cautious assumption running the wrong way.

challenges.challenge: The scenario, bear/bull and reverse-DCF values are not computed on the base case’s price path. Reproduce: a x1.0 multiplier on d.agri.cpo returns a DCF of Rp3,904/share against the reported base of Rp5,167, because the override writes the long-run price (USD1,180) flat into FY2030E-FY2035E instead of escalating at 2.5%; the CPO/FX sensitivity grid’s centre cell is Rp3,773 against the stated base target of Rp4,774. The bear (1,827), bull (6,254), probability-weighted 4,407, the target 3,085 and the implied benchmark 1,194 are therefore not comparable with the DCF, and the market-prices-the-deck-as-we-do conclusion is an artefact of the override.
challenges.answer: Confirmed engine defect: the scenario, sensitivity and reverse-DCF overrides write the deck long run flat beyond the explicit FY2029E path, so a multiplier of one does not reproduce the base DCF. Scripts are outside this desk edit rights. The sensitivity grids, the scenario table and the implied benchmark are withdrawn and the defect is disclosed in sections 4 and 5; the rating now rests on the primary DCF net of the liquidity discount.

challenges.challenge: The report never states the price at which control changed hands. S6: 768m Pinago shares at Rp3,600 each for USD162m, i.e. Rp3,600/share; the file’s own valuation.post_bs_review adds a July mandatory tender at Rp3,584. Both are 16-17% above the Rp3,085 target and about 10% above the Rp3,260 price. The report calls a follow-on tender the only realistic liquidity event without giving its price, and treats the parent’s price as unknowable when the only observed parent price is above the market.
challenges.answer: The control price is now stated in sections 5 and 6 via fact F22 (768m shares at Rp3,600 for USD162m, S6) and the July mandatory tender is disclosed as clearing within one per cent of it. A new section 6 subsection reconciles a minority target with the block price: control premium plus the 30% liquidity discount on a 0.52% float; the exact Rp3,584 tender is recorded in qc_justifications valuation.control_price.

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says the acquisition announcement explicitly framed the tender as not leading to a delisting [S6]. S6 contains no reference to delisting; it says only that AEP must run a mandatory tender for the remaining shares, estimated at USD3m. The statement is fabricated as a citation and it is load-bearing: it is the sole support for the claim that the listing survives.
challenges.answer: The delisting sentence is removed. S6 contains no reference to delisting, so the citation was fabricated. Section 6 now states plainly that we searched the source record and found no delisting undertaking from the parent: the listing survives for now with no commitment to keep it.

challenges.challenge: Opex is 7.70% of revenue (FY2026E Rp189.7bn) against S4 p.7’s H1-2026 G&A of Rp131.1bn on revenue of Rp1,116.6bn (11.7%) plus selling of Rp10.8bn - about Rp275bn annualised ex-D&A, Rp85bn above the model. The jump is salaries and allowances (Rp84.0bn vs Rp44.9bn), a recurring line, and the assumption’s dismissal as transaction and integration cost around the change of control cites no note or page. At the H1 run rate FY2026E net profit falls roughly 19% and the target falls to about Rp2,650, a REDUCE rather than a HOLD.
challenges.answer: No note or page discloses a one-off, so the run rate is carried. H1-2026 G&A 131.12 plus selling 10.84 less G&A depreciation 4.60 = 137.36 on revenue 1,116.56, i.e. 12.3%, annualised 274.7bn. opex_pct moves from 7.70% to 12.3% for all forecast years. Rating HOLD to REDUCE, target 3,085 to 2,617, total return +0.1% to -15.7%.

challenges.challenge: The cost allocation contradicts note 36. The model’s non-CPO block carries Rp413.7bn of cost against Rp809.7bn of revenue (48.9% margin), but the rubber segment alone - Rp541.5bn of that block’s revenue - had COGS of Rp479.4bn (11.5% margin, S3 p.102). A block containing all of rubber cannot cost less than rubber alone; at least Rp65.8bn (Rp621k/t, 5.1% of unit cost) of the CPO pool belongs to rubber. The model’s margin split (CPO 15.5%, other 48.9%) inverts the filing’s (palm 27.6%, rubber 11.5%).
challenges.answer: The shared Rp245.378bn estate pool is allocated on the segment note: rubber carries 479.4bn of cost on 541.5bn revenue (11.5% margin), so Rp65.758bn of processing and estate cost moved out of the CPO pool. CPO cash cost is now 1,143.4bn, or Rp10.801m/t; cost_per_bcm and other_margin (40.78%) are re-derived.

challenges.challenge: Volume is held at 107kt for ten years on the assertion that the estate is not expanding and the mill is already near capacity. AR p.88 shows the palm nucleus is 16,139ha of which 4,342ha (27%) is immature, and own FFB was 161,436t on 11,797ha mature - a normal 13.7 t/ha, not a mature-estate ceiling. S6 gives the mill at 120 t/h, or 600-790kt/yr of FFB against 461kt processed (58-77% utilisation). The immature block is a sourced volume pipeline the base case ignores.
challenges.answer: Volume is rebuilt on the immature roll-forward: 4,342 ha of 16,139 immature (27%), own FFB 161,436t on 11,797 ha mature at 13.7 t/ha, mill 120 t/h against 461kt processed (58-77% utilisation). FY2026E-FY2030E volume is 107.0/108.5/110.0/111.5/113.0 kt, taking half the gross maturation because replanting offsets it.

challenges.challenge: The report’s central risk is the 0.52% free float, yet it omits the exchange’s 15% minimum. The registry in the model file records free_float 0.52%, min 15%, gap 14.48pp, deadline 2029-03-31. Meeting it requires the parent to place or sell roughly 113m shares (14.5% of capital, around 17,000 days of current ADTV) or a rights issue - a supply event and the most plausible route to restoring liquidity. The no-exit thesis is incomplete without it.
challenges.answer: Sections 5 and 6 now state the 15% minimum free float, the 14.48pp gap and the 31 March 2029 deadline, and size the required sell-down at roughly 113m shares (or a rights issue). It is presented as both an overhang that supports the discount and the one credible route to float restoration; section 7 monitors progress.

challenges.challenge: The non-CPO block (Rp842.1bn FY2026E, growing 4% then 3%/yr) is part kernel but largely rubber, and rubber production has collapsed from 31,841t (2023) to 23,733t (2024) to 14,779t (2025) - minus 54% in two years (AR p.90). The model grows the block with the vegetable-oil complex plus 2.5% inflation at a 48.9% margin, with no volume source and no discussion of the decline; the report says only that crumb rubber volume was down sharply.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now splits the non-CPO block: it is mostly rubber, with production 31,841t (2023), 23,733t (2024), 14,779t (2025), down 54% in two years. Other revenue is held flat in real terms rather than grown, and other_margin is reconciled to the segment note at 40.78%.

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle CPO anchor (USD1,150/t) and the deck path (USD1,240) - the most important valuation input - are cited to S0, which is Yahoo Finance statements and prices, not the deck; the World Bank Pink Sheet, FCPO strip and MPOC sources named in the deck’s own basis appear nowhere. The WACC inputs (rf 7.45%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, spread 2.0%) are uncited. Separately, the report calls the FCPO strip in backwardation and above the nearby contract, but the deck’s own strip rises from RM4,587 (Nov-26) to RM5,030 (Apr-27), which is contango.
challenges.answer: Section 2 cites the agri deck and names its primary sources, the World Bank Pink Sheet series, Harga Referensi, the Bursa FCPO strip and MPOC. Section 4 cites the macro deck for the risk-free rate, ERP and CRP and names Damodaran; kd is the pack three-year average. The strip is described as rising through H1-2027, which is contango, not backwardation.

challenges.challenge: The BLOCK calibration flag (-23.4%: model EBITDA 374.9 vs actual 489.5) is justified only by the benchmark re-basing. The arithmetic shows roughly two-thirds of the gap is cost, not price: the engine prices FY2025 at the FY2026E unit cost of Rp12,147,500/t, which is Rp725,500/t above the analyst’s own note-derived FY2025 cash cost of Rp11.422m/t (Rp76.8bn on 105.858kt). FY2025A EBITDA also adds back only the Rp52.7bn of depreciation, not the Rp14.2bn bearer-plant amortisation that FY2026E D&A includes (489.5 vs 503.7-511.2), so history and forecast sit on different D&A definitions.
challenges.answer: qc_justifications calibration.ebitda now reconciles line by line: model 260.6 against actual 489.5, a 46.8% gap; price and FX about -70.8 (gross price -161.7 offset by FX +90.9), unit cost about -74.9 at 11.509m against 10.801m per tonne, opex about -97.3 with 13.9bn of historical G&A depreciation moving inside opex. Aligning the actual to the forecast D&A definition by adding the 14.2bn bearer amortisation gives 503.7bn.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies 5.83x to Rp532.7bn, which is the data pack’s LTM EBITDA (datapack ltm.ebitda = 532.687) - trailing, and on the pack’s understated-D&A basis that the report’s own section 3 says overstates EBITDA. The prose calls it the blended forward number, which it is not; on FY2026E EBITDA of 544.0 the leg would be about Rp3,957. The 5.83x is the mean of the peer median (about 6.1x) and a four-observation own average (5.56x).
challenges.answer: The EV leg is relabelled as the pack trailing LTM EBITDA on the understated-D&A basis and disclosed as a floor, not a forward number. The multiple is described as the config blend of peer median and own five-year mean; the prose no longer calls it a blended forward number.

challenges.challenge: The HOLD does not survive the checklist’s bear-weight test. At the delivered values (base 4,444, bear 1,697, bull 5,885), doubling the bear to 50% gives a weighted value of Rp3,431, a target of Rp2,402 and a total return of -20.8%, a REDUCE; a 35% bear weight gives -12.0%, also a REDUCE. The 25% bear weight is therefore the only thing holding the rating, yet the bear case is the one the report’s own section 2 (GAPKI 2027) calls the most important industry fact.
challenges.answer: With the H1-2026 cost run rate carried, the engine is REDUCE at the 25% bear weight, so the rating no longer rests on the weight. Section 5 discloses the weight sensitivity and states that a third or a half on the bear is more negative, and justifies a quarter because the deck path already embeds the GAPKI 2027 warning.

challenges.challenge: The P/BV passage is not substantive enough to justify keeping the leg. The 1.42x is the average of the peer median (about 1.27x) and the own four-year mean (1.58x), so where-this-stock-has-traded-because-the-float-has-been-thin explains at most half of it. The report’s own warranted multiple, (ROE-g)/(COE-g) = (0.27-0.025)/(0.115-0.025) = 2.7x, is nearly double the 1.42x used. The text calls the leg circular but keeps its 15% weight; dropping it and re-weighting the DCF/EV legs takes the blended value from 4,444 to about 4,787 and the target up about Rp240.
challenges.answer: The P/BV leg is dropped and the weights renormalised to 70% DCF and 30% EV/EBITDA. Its placeholders and prose are removed, and the passage that called the leg circular while keeping it is replaced with a statement that the leg is gone.

challenges.challenge: Three citations do not hold: the July 2026 renaming is cited to S2, but the AR-2025 text contains no AEP or Pinago Plantations (the deal closed after the AR); the 0.52% free float is cited to S0 but comes from the IDX registry; and carbon trading named as an emerging adjacency [S2] is not in S2, whose relevant page refers only to emissions reduction. Separately, the de-numbered prose renders duplicate units (USD 162 USD mm, USD US$1,194/t, 461 kt kt, Rp542 IDR bnbn), and the all-sales-are-domestic framing is contradicted by S2 p.86, which says rubber export receipts are in USD and give natural hedging.
challenges.answer: The renaming and the free float are re-cited to the desk IDX registry (the annual report predates the deal), the carbon-trading claim is removed and replaced with emissions reduction, duplicated units are fixed across the report, and the FX paragraph now acknowledges the USD rubber export receipts on S2 page 86.

challenges.challenge: The realisation the model runs is published as 0.8 in two places while the assumptions and section 2 say 0.76: section 3 renders in.realisation.FY2026E as 0.8 of the deck benchmark, and section 7 sets the KPI as testing whether 0.8 is still the right ratio. At 1,135 x 0.8 the reader gets USD 908/t against the model 862.6, a 5 pct error in the top line on the single input the house calibrates realisation on.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now renders the realisation as 0.76 of the deck benchmark (num2 format) and section 7 tests 76% (pct0), so both reproduce the 0.76 the model runs for FY2026E through the long run, matching section 2 and fund record [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 7 publishes a per-share bear value of Rp1,901 as the downside, while sections 4 and 5 state that no per-share tail value is published because the engine scenario override does not run on the base price path, and the withdrawn grid CPO x1.0 cell prints 2,844 against the 4,013 base. The one downside number in the report therefore rests on exactly the defect the report disowns.
challenges.answer: Deleted the per-share bear value from section 7. The downside is now stated in EBITDA terms - roughly a third off the FY2027E EBITDA placeholder - on the corrected cost pass-through, and section 5 publishes that same treatment only, so no withheld-grid value is used anywhere [S3].

challenges.challenge: The scenario cost shocks are derived from 0.645, the FFB line ratio to realised CPO price (9.103/14.115), not from the FFB line share of unit cost, which is 9.103 of 10.802 or 84 pct. On the model own cost formula a 20 pct benchmark move re-prices unit cost to 0.828x/1.172x, not 0.871x/1.129x, so the tails overstate the bear spread compression and the section 5 statement that the shocks re-price at the model own pass-through is false, as are the tail EBITDA figures built from them.
challenges.answer: Re-derived the cost shocks from the base cost formula at the FY2027E cost base, not from the FFB/revenue ratio: 1.7415 + 11.1989 x 0.8 on 12.9404 = 0.828 bear and 1.172 bull, replacing 0.871/1.129. Section 5 now says unit cost falls about a sixth with the benchmark and EBITDA moves roughly a third each way [S3].

missing_bull_case.note: The freshest arm’s-length price evidence is omitted: AEP paid Rp3,600/share in May 2026 (S6: 768m shares x Rp3.6 = USD162m) and the file’s own post_bs_review records a Rp3,584 tender - both well above the Rp3,085 target (C2). Also absent: 4,342 ha (27%) of the palm nucleus is immature (AR p.88), a sourced volume pipeline the flat-volume base ignores (C6); and float restoration could close the discount (C7). Credit: the mill-versus-estate spread logic and the D&A restatement are right.

missing_bear_case.note: Omitted: AR p.84 says the government plans to raise the CPO export levy in 2026, which lowers the domestic reference the company sells at and the 0.76 realisation with it; the 15% minimum free float (0.52% actual, 14.48pp gap, deadline 2029-03-31) implies a mandated sell-down or rights issue (C7); rubber production fell from 31,841t (2023) to 14,779t (2025) while the model grows the other-revenue block 3-4%/yr (C8); and the SG&A step-up is dismissed without a source (C4). Credit: the shocks are genuinely mirrored and leverage is correctly shown to be small.

assumption_realism.note: Of the three value drivers: realisation 0.76 is sourced and matches the LTM arithmetic; volume flat at 107kt is contradicted by the 27% immature nucleus and an unsourced near-capacity claim (C6); cost per tonne is built from the note but the allocation puts the rubber segment’s own COGS (479.4) inside the CPO pool, inverting the filing’s segment margins (C5); and SG&A at 7.70% of revenue assumes the H1-2026 11.7% G&A ratio halves with no source (C4).

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checked S2, S3, S4 and S6: F1/F3/F5/F7/F8/F9/F15/F17/F18/F19 all support their numbers; F12 total depreciation 52,704,525,846 is correctly read, and notes 28/29/36 reconcile to revenue and COGS. But the not-leading-to-a-delisting line is not in S6 (C3); the renaming is cited to S2, which contains no AEP (C14); and the deck/WACC inputs are cited to S0 (Yahoo) or not at all, with the FCPO strip called backwardation when it is rising (C9).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary at 60% is right for a finite-life plantation, the 47% TV share on 2.5% growth is acceptable and net debt/minorities are bridged at 30-Sep-2026. The defect is that the scenario/bear/bull/reverse-DCF machinery is not on the base path: a x1.0 CPO override returns DCF 3,904 vs the reported 5,167 and the sensitivity grid centre is 3,773 vs the base 4,774 (C1); EV/EBITDA uses trailing pack EBITDA (C11); and the WACC kd of 9.45% contradicts the 6.11% cost_of_debt in the same file.

bias_and_tone.note: Candid about the narrow variant view, but the central claim that the gap is the price of having almost no float is contradicted by the reverse DCF, which says the price is consistent with a benchmark only 3.7% below the deck - i.e. no float discount in the price at all (C1/C9). The HOLD does not survive doubling the bear weight: a 50% bear gives -20.8% total return, a REDUCE (C12). The P/BV passage argues the leg is circular yet keeps 15% weight on it (C13).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right deck variables: d.agri.cpo in USD against an IDR cost base, realisation 0.76 inside the peer band (LSIP 0.758), no royalty on domestic CPO sales, and 2.5% IDR inflation applied consistently to cost escalation and terminal growth. Peer multiples are averaged with the own history as the config sets. No deck-variable inconsistency; the failure is in the override mechanics, not the inputs (C1).

conservatism_audit.note: Below-actual or below-disclosure inputs: volume flat for ten years against a 4,342ha immature pipeline (C6); opex 7.70% of revenue vs the audited 7.37% ex-D&A and the H1-2026 11.7% G&A ratio (C4); capex held at 1.158m/t with 3,957ha of palms over 14 years due for replanting; FY2025A EBITDA excludes the 14.2bn bearer-plant amortisation that forecast D&A includes (C10); DPS 179 vs the last declared 90. The shock set itself is symmetric, so there is no mirrored-shock asymmetry to challenge.

calibration.note: The single BLOCK flag is justified but only for the benchmark re-basing. The -23.4% gap (model 374.9 vs actual 489.5) is also mechanical: the engine prices FY2025 at the FY2026E cost of 12,147,500/t, Rp725,500/t (Rp76.8bn, ~67% of the gap) above the analyst’s own note-derived FY2025 cash cost of 11.422m/t, and FY2025A EBITDA adds back only 52.7bn of depreciation, not the 14.2bn bearer amortisation that FY2026E D&A includes. Credit: the NP/OCF reconciliation is right - 553.9 vs 322.6 and 363.8 vs 221.0, so no accruals flag.

signoff.notes: HOLD, TP 2,808 on 3,260 (-9.8 pct). Base is most-likely, not cautious: realisation 0.76 is not a haircut but the like-for-like LTM calibration (about Rp15.2m/t against deck 9M-2026 USD1,131 at 17,570) re-solved from the H1-2026 mix, and it matches the desk LSIP 0.758; the FY2025 0.852 sits on the pre-rebase series the deck flags. H1-2026 opex run rate carried with no one-off claimed; capex, payout and tax at last actual. The HOLD rests on the disclosed 30 pct liquidity discount for a 0.52 pct float and IDR21.4m ADTV, consistent with fund record, and the report says so plainly. Scenario-order defect is a documented engine override, disclosed with zero weights and no published per-share tail. Q1/Q2 are text-level and do not move a readers number; Q3 sensitivity is advice only.

bias.note: Base re-prices FY2025A at last-actual economics with no unsourced haircut: volume 107kt FY2026E flat on 105.858kt [F1/S2], cost at the FY2025 note [S3], opex carried at the H1-2026 run rate though it is the cautious reading [S4], realisation 0.76 vs the 0.852 FY2025 ratio but supported line by line by the LTM test (Rp2,480.5bn LTM revenue [S0], 64.9% CPO share, Rp19.87m/t deck) and disclosed in s2-s4. No unsourced optimism either: volume adds only half the immature maturation. Tails mirrored 0.8/1.2 price, 0.95/1.05 volume, 0.828/1.172 cost and carry zero weight.

findings.finding: s6 Dividend record says declared DPS ran from Rp130 to Rp90 across the four years; the pack [S0] shows ex-dates of Rp40, Rp130 and Rp90 in 2024-2026 and fiscal sums of Rp130 (2023), Rp92 (2024), Rp170 (2025), so the stated range contradicts the payout basis that cites the same source.

Placeholder-plus-typed-unit remains after the C14 fix: s6 prints "a maximum of 13.6 m shares million shares" and s1 prints "19,952 ha hectares", "11,797 ha hectares", "4,342 ha hectares" and "19,147 ha hectares"; the values are right, the units read as a bug.

Realisation 0.76 is 11% under the FY2025 audited ratio 0.852; the LTM CPO-revenue share used (64.9% of revenue) is the FY2025 mix while H1-2026 palm+pallet revenue is 79.6% of the half, so a mix-updated ratio would be nearer 0.85. The rating is unaffected (0.85 leaves HOLD), but the report should say so rather than let the level sit on one mix assumption.

Bull scenario value (3,578) is below base (4,012) because of the documented override defect; the zero weights and the absence of any published per-share tail are the right treatment, but the engine defect should be logged for the platform owner so the next round can restore a weighted blend.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 260.6 vs the actual 489.5 (-47%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gate re-prices FY2025 at the FY2026E benchmark of USD 1,135/t and FY2025A volume of 105.858kt, and the gap (model about 260.6 vs actual 489.5, roughly -47%) decomposes line by line, not only by the benchmark re-basing. Price and FX about -70.8bn: realisation 0.76 on the 2026-series benchmark gives about Rp12,488m/t against the FY2025 realised Rp14,115m/t [S2], partly offset by the FY2026 rate of Rp17,570 against the FY2025 average of Rp16,448; gross price effect about -161.7bn and FX about +90.9bn. Unit cost about -74.9bn: the re-pricing carries the FY2026 estate cost of Rp11.509m/t over 105.858kt, while the FY2025 cash cost per the note was Rp10.801m/t [S3]. Opex about -97.3bn: the FY2026 rate of 12.3% of revenue from the H1-2026 run rate [S4] against the FY2025 actual of 177.4bn ex-depreciation, with about 13.9bn of G&A depreciation moving back inside opex. Definition: FY2025A EBITDA adds back only 52.7bn of fixed-asset depreciation, while forecast D&A also includes the 14.2bn bearer-plant amortisation [S3]; aligning the actual to the forecast definition gives 503.7bn rather than 489.5bn. The residual is that FY2025 was a high-price, low-cost year: the calibration measures a re-pricing, not a forecast that is too low.

flags.message: probabilities bear 0% / base 100% / bull 0%: base below 40% or a tail below 10%
flags.justification: The twelve-month target is the base method blend rolled forward at the cost of equity, Rp4,013.5, less the house 30% liquidity discount, Rp2,809.4 - one path, reproducible from the assumptions line by line - and it is not a probability blend. The bear and bull runs are published as driver sensitivities at zero weight because the engine's scenario override writes the deck long run flat beyond the last explicit year: every shocked run sits on a lower price path than the valuation (a x1.0 multiplier returns about 2,485 against the 4,013 base), so blending them into the target would publish a number no model reproduces, which is exactly the round-1 BLOCK Q1 defect. The likelihoods of the states are stated in section five in words with their drivers [S5], and the shocks are mirrored (0.8/1.2 on the deck, 0.95/1.05 on volume) and re-price the bought-fruit line with the benchmark at the base cost formula's own pass-through: 0.828x and 1.172x, derived at the FY2027E cost base, replaced the earlier 0.871/1.129 that came from the FFB line's ratio to realised price rather than its share of unit cost [S3].

flags.message: scenario values are not ordered bear <= base <= bull
flags.justification: Disclosed, not fixed, and it is the same override defect: the engine writes the CPO deck flat beyond the explicit FY2029E path before applying the shock, while the a.cost_per_bcm multiplier applies to the whole cost path. In the bull the bought-fruit line carries 1.172x unit cost on every year, including the terminal years where the price premium has been truncated, and because that line is about 86% of FY2027E unit cost [S3] the cost effect outweighs the 5% volume uplift: the bull prints 3,357 against the 3,717 base, so bear <= base <= bull fails on the engine, not on the assumptions. The shocks themselves are correct and mirrored (0.8/1.2 deck, 0.95/1.05 volume, 0.828/1.172 cost from the base cost formula); no per-share tail value is published and both tails carry zero weight in the target, which is the base method blend at Rp4,012 less the liquidity discount.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The P/BV leg was dropped because its multiple is a blend of a peer median and a four-year own-history mean for a stock whose float has never been normal, so it measures the register rather than the business; the DCF and EV/EBITDA weights absorb its 15% proportionally, at 70 and 30. The EV leg is kept as a cross-check only, on the pack trailing EBITDA, and is disclosed as a floor because the pack D&A is understated [S0].
